title: UniFi operator site profile
description: Operator-supplied intent a UniFi controller cannot report about itself: trust roles, criticality, ownership, intended policies, and operational constraints. The profile is optional; a package with no profile runs in discovery-only mode and infers none of these. Credentials are excluded by this schema rather than by convention, by value as well as by name: every object is closed, every property name is checked against credential-shaped names, and every free-text value is checked against literal credential formats. Version 1.1 adds no field and removes none; it records that the secret-free guarantee now covers values. A 1.0 document remains readable and is held to the same value rule, because a credential in a 1.0 profile is exactly as exposed. The entropy-graded half of the value rule - a credential-shaped key assigned a high-entropy value - is expressible in code but not in JSON Schema, and is enforced by the loader in ../scripts/site_profile.py; see ../references/site-profile.md for the exact wording of the guarantee.

schema_version.description: Contract version of this document. An unrecognized version is rejected outright rather than partially applied.

subjects.description: Things at the site the operator has an intent about. A subject absent from this list has no known intent; that absence is reported as unknown and is never filled in from observation.

intended_policies.description: Policies the operator means to hold. Comparing them to controller state is a drift report, not an enforcement action.

operational_constraints.description: Standing constraints on how the site may be operated.

nonCredentialPropertyName.description: Property names are lower snake case and may not be credential-shaped. A site profile carries intent; a secret in it would be a secret in whatever repository or backup the profile reaches.

identifier.description: A stable operator-chosen name. Not required to match any controller-assigned identifier.

credentialFreeText.description: Non-empty free text that is not itself a credential. Property names are guarded separately; this guards the value, so a secret does not become acceptable by being written into a field whose name is innocent. Each rejected pattern is a literal well-known credential format. There is deliberately no bare high-entropy rejection: a profile legitimately carries digests and long identifiers, and a check that fires on those is a check an operator turns off.

trustRole.description: How much the operator intends to trust a subject. The literal unknown is permitted and means the same as omitting the field.

criticality.description: How much the operator intends a subject to matter. The literal unknown is permitted and means the same as omitting the field.

applies_to.description: Subject identifiers this policy is meant to cover.
